claims.text: Preheating the SLM build chamber reduces the thermal gradient between the melt pool and surrounding material.
Reducing thermal gradients through chamber preheating reduces fabrication-induced defects in SLM-produced HEAs.
Chamber preheating improves the dimensional precision of SLM-produced HEA components relative to room-temperature fabrication.
Chamber preheating enhances the mechanical integrity of SLM-produced HEA components relative to room-temperature fabrication.
HEA parts produced by SLM at ambient chamber temperature typically experience high cooling rates.
Ambient-temperature SLM of HEAs typically produces residual stresses, layer mismatches, and microstructural inhomogeneities.
Residual stresses, layer mismatches, and microstructural inhomogeneities lead to porosity and microcracking in SLM-produced HEAs.
A chamber temperature in the range of 200–300°C is an appropriate example of an optimized preheating regime for HEA SLM.
The elevated chamber temperature should be maintained throughout the SLM build.
The proposed preheating intervention is applicable to HEAs made from either elemental powder mixtures or pre-alloyed powders.
A lower thermal gradient caused by preheating produces a slower cooling rate.
Slower cooling promotes more uniform layer fusion and minimizes residual-stress accumulation.
Preheating produces a more homogeneous microstructure with reduced porosity and fewer microcracks.
Reduced cooling rates moderate thermal contraction and thereby limit warping and residual stresses.
Build-chamber preheating enhances metallurgical bonding between SLM layers.
Microstructural homogenization reduces the likelihood of defect nucleation.
Preheated samples will have less warping, less layer misalignment, lower porosity, and less microcracking than room-temperature controls.
Preheated samples will have higher tensile strength and improved ductility relative to room-temperature controls.
Excessively high preheating temperatures may cause grain coarsening or undesirable phase transformations.
The optimal preheating temperature depends on HEA composition, powder characteristics, thermal properties, and machine characteristics.
